place.en: Johari Bazaar · a goldsmith’s strongroom · 3:20 AM

brief.en: Farida’s strongroom was opened at twenty past three without a scratch on the lock. Her day book is gone and so are forty books of gold leaf. She says one person did this. The dust on the floor says two.

iraNote.en: “Two sets of prints in the gold dust. One of them stopped and came back for a second look — that’s the one who wasn’t expecting company.”

text.en: Sealing wax in the third lever, cut with lamp black. Same block as the Gangauri tiffin.
Two sets of prints in the gold dust. One pair went in and out. One pair went in, stopped, and came back for a second look.
Page 41 was torn before the book left. The stub still reads: “L — 900 — Teej”.
The dancer’s set finished at 2:40. The bazaar is a four-minute walk.
Bolted from the inside. The bolt is oiled and the oil is still wet.
Forty books in on the 14th. Booked out the same night on the 11:40 goods seat to Mumbai. Consignee left blank.
One bell, and the sill dust beneath it is unbroken. It landed after the dust had settled.

label.en: THE ONLY KEY · ON ITS CORD

text.en: Round the goldsmith’s neck all night. Her husband will swear to it.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — she never let go of the key, which is exactly why nobody needed it

text.en: The durwan’s. Reported lost for the second time this month.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a man who loses the same stud twice is careless, not clever

text.en: Pigeons up off the arch all at once. Something moved under them.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — birds go up for cats too

hook.en: her strongroom · her key · her loss

alibi.en: The only key was on her neck all night, which is the point — nobody needed it.

confession.en: Nine hundred owed since Teej, and a day book that said so. She found the strongroom already open, took the page she came for, and went out over the roof. The gold was gone before she arrived.

hook.en: his stud, on the shop step, again

alibi.en: On the haveli gate eleven streets away, and this time the register is in somebody else’s hand.

hook.en: delivered a crate to this step last week

alibi.en: Asleep at the rickshaw stand, where the chowkidar kicks him awake at four and did.

hook.en: the gold leaf was hers, and insured

alibi.en: Her leaf, her order, her loss. Nobody breaks into a strongroom to rob themselves — and her claim was never filed.

correction.en: A key on a woman’s neck is not a motive. Nine hundred rupees owed since Teej is.
That stud has been on the step a fortnight. A set that finished at 2:40 four minutes away has not.
Pigeons don’t tell you how anyone left. There is a hatch in that roof and somebody oiled the bolt.

text.en: “The key never left my neck. Not to sleep, not to wash.”
“There are a great many L’s in Jaipur.” She did not say the debt was not hers.
“Somebody has spent my gold on a train ticket. How very like this family.”

setting.en: Behind her own counter, with the strongroom door open behind her.

ask.en: Who else knew the leaf was in there?

answer.en: “Whoever wrote the consignment note. Half the bazaar handles those.”

note.en: Half the bazaar — and exactly one of them cast a key.

ask.en: There is sealing wax in the third lever.

answer.en: “Then somebody made a key. I have the only one and I have never let go of it.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the lab slip on the lock. The wax is the question.

note.en: She never let go of it, which is precisely why nobody needed it.

ask.en: Two sets of prints in the gold dust.

answer.en: “Then two people. The one who came for the leaf, and the one who came for my book.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the strongroom floor. Two sets of prints is a photograph, not a feeling.

note.en: Two people, an hour apart — and only one of them knew the other had been.

setting.en: A rehearsal room in Johari, at noon, with the tabla still out.

ask.en: What time did the wedding set finish?

answer.en: “Twenty to three. The band card will say so.”

note.en: Twenty to three. The strongroom was standing open at twenty past.

answer.en: “There are a great many L’s in Jaipur.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the day book’s stub — the page is the only thing she has to answer for.

note.en: There are. There is one who owed nine hundred since Teej and finished work four minutes away.

ask.en: A bell on the sill, on dust that had already settled.

answer.en: “I have lost bells in six districts. It proves I was somewhere, once.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the ghungroo. The dust under it is the whole point of it.

note.en: Once. The dust says after three in the morning.

setting.en: Her own courtyard. She does not offer you a chair.

answer.en: “Naturally. And no claim has been filed, before you ask.”

note.en: No claim. Whatever this was, it was not for the insurance.

answer.en: “My steward, on my order, for Teej. It was to be beaten into a canopy.”

note.en: So the leaf’s route was written down where anybody in the bazaar could read it.

ask.en: It was booked out on the 11:40 the same night.

answer.en: “Then somebody has spent my gold on a train ticket. How very like this family.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the consignment note — the booking is what she has to be told about.

note.en: “This family.” She said it before she had thought about it.

bankedClue.en: A goods seat on the 11:40 to Mumbai, consignee left blank

text.en: Two people were in that room an hour apart. Which of them finished work at 2:40, four minutes away?
